report.source_text: The treatment started with intravenous methylprednisolon in dose of 500 mg for 3 days and intravenous cyclophosphamid in dose of 0.6 g/1 m² of body surface 6 times in 4-week intervals with low molecular weight heparin, enalapril, amlodypine, spironolacton, venlafaxine and carbamazepine administered too. At present, the treatment is continued in 8-week intervals with the usage of prednisone 10 mg/d, low molecular weight heparin, hypotension drugs, carbamazepine and venlafaxine. Prophylaxis of osteoporosis and against alimentary tract complications is continued. After 8-month treatment the condition of the patient is good. There is still hypertension but the symptoms of polyneuropathy are less visible though there has been muscular atrophy in both hands observed. Control EMG examination has shown slow regeneration process and beginning of reinnervation changes in checked muscles. Abdominal pains have disappeared and there is the gain of weight. In laboratory test there are still anemia (Hb 11.6 g/dl) and lymphopenia (700/mm³).

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 53-year-old woman presented with overlapping systemic autoimmune features including sicca symptoms (xerostomia, xeromycteria), sensomotor polyneuropathy, abdominal pains, hypertension, headaches, and weight loss. Initial workup confirmed primary Sjögren's syndrome through positive anti-Ro/SSA antibodies, positive Schirmer's test, and lower lip salivary gland biopsy demonstrating focal lymphoid infiltration with periductal fibroma (Greenspan IV°). Concurrent evaluation for systemic vasculitis revealed elevated inflammatory markers (ESR 60 mm/h, CRP 10.9 mg/dl, lymphopenia), multiple visceral artery stenoses on CT angiography (40% right renal, 50% superior mesenteric, 30% left common iliac), and EMG demonstrating primary axonal sensomotor polyneuropathy with features of fresh massive lesion consistent with mononeuritis multiplex. The patient was treated with intravenous methylprednisolone (500 mg × 3 days) followed by cyclophosphamide (0.6 g/m² × 6 doses at 4-week intervals), with maintenance therapy including prednisone and immunosuppression. After 8 months, she demonstrated good clinical response with resolution of abdominal pains, weight gain, and improving polyneuropathy (EMG showing regeneration/reinnervation), though hypertension and mild anemia persisted.
